raw: | `mxcli check … --references` reports "nanoflow not found: Mod.Flow" for a nanoflow created **earlier in the same script**, printed directly under the line "(Note: References to objects created within the script are skipped)". `exec` runs the same file without complaint and `mx check` is 0 errors | `mdl/executor/helpers.go` (`validateWidgetReferences`) | One omission in a list of five. The function consults `sc.<kind>` — the same-script exemption — for microflows, pages, snippets and entities, and for **nanoflows alone** it did not, so every widget reference kind was exempt except that one. Fix is `&& !sc.nanoflows[ref]`, matching its four siblings. Note this is the **inverse** of MDL-ORDER01, which exists to catch a reference to something created *later*; a rule pair like that is worth checking in both directions when one half is added. The test asserts all the kinds in one table so the omission cannot reappear on a different line, and the control is a nanoflow in neither the project nor the script, which must still be reported. Reported as ledger #138; example `mdl-examples/bug-tests/ledger-138-snippet-nanoflow-same-script.mdl` |
